etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: First use appears c. 1646. From Medieval Latin asceticus, from Ancient Greek ἀσκητικός (askētikós), from ἀσκητής (askētḗs, “monk, hermit”), from ἀσκέω (askéō, “to exercise”).
senses: Characterized by rigorous self-denial or self-discipline; austere; abstinent; involving a withholding of physical pleasure.
One who is devoted to the practice of self-denial, either through seclusion or stringent abstinence.
